attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

null-vs-empty.notApplicableReason: Every text column of StateProvince and CountryRegion is NOT NULL, so no NULL text value can be sent; '' is attacked as an empty country code and an empty nchar(3) province code.

cases.label: case pairs outside ASCII ('üs' to 'ÜS', 'σa' to 'ΣA') and case plus a trailing space on the country side ('CA' to 'ca ')
cases.reasoning: The hand-derived cases join an ASCII lowercase province code to an uppercase country and a province code with a trailing space; both differences sit on the province side. Here the case pairs are Latin-1 (ü/Ü) and Greek (σ/Σ), which CI_AS folds through its Unicode case tables, and the country row itself is lowercase with a trailing space ('ca '), so the rtrim and the case-insensitive comparison must apply to the country side too. A conversion that lower()ed only ASCII, folded with a byte-wise or C-collation upper(), or trimmed only the province side would drop rows that SQL Server keeps. These are valid source rows: CountryRegion keys 'ÜS', 'ΣA' and 'ca ' are distinct under the case-insensitive key, and each province code references its country under that collation.

cases.label: expansions: province code 'Æ' against country 'AE' and 'ß' against 'SS', with 'ae' and 'ss' as case-only controls
cases.reasoning: Windows collation rules (used by SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS for nvarchar) treat 'Æ' as equal to 'AE' and 'ß' as equal to 'ss'. The ICU root collation at strength 2 gives 'æ' its own primary weight (not equal to 'ae') while 'ß' = 'ss' differs only at the tertiary level. The engines may disagree on whether the 'Æ' province joins.

cases.label: compatibility forms: full-width U+FF35 U+FF33 against 'US' and the Kelvin sign U+212A followed by 'E' against 'KE', with 'ke' as a case-only control
cases.reasoning: SQL Server collations without _WS are width-insensitive, so full-width 'ＵＳ' equals 'US'; U+212A KELVIN SIGN is canonically equivalent to 'K'. ICU at strength 2 ignores width (a tertiary difference) and normalises canonical equivalents. Either engine may treat one of these differently.

cases.label: whitespace look-alikes: 'US' with a trailing no-break space (U+00A0), a trailing tab, a leading space, a soft hyphen (U+00AD) inside, and 'CA ' (a real trailing space)
cases.reasoning: SQL Server pads the shorter value with U+0020 before comparing, so only 'CA ' is certain to join. Whether U+00A0 compares equal to the pad space, and whether the soft hyphen U+00AD is ignorable, are collation rules; PostgreSQL rtrim(' ') removes U+0020 only and ICU treats U+00AD as ignorable and U+00A0 as a space variant. A tab and a leading space should join on neither engine.

cases.label: accents and dotted/dotless I: 'ÜS' against 'US' (accent-sensitive); U+0131 and U+0130 followed by 'T' against 'IT', with 'it' as a case-only control
cases.reasoning: CI_AS is accent-sensitive, so 'ÜS' must not join 'US'. U+0131 (dotless i) and U+0130 (I with dot above) case-fold differently by rule set: Windows rules and ICU root may each match or not match 'IT'. 'it' joins on both.

cases.label: an empty country code: province codes '' and ' ' both join country '' (trailing spaces ignored)
cases.reasoning: SQL Server compares '' and ' ' as equal (padding), so both provinces join the country whose code is ''. rtrim(' ') gives '' on PostgreSQL; this checks the empty-string edge of the rtrim + ICU equality and that '' is not treated as NULL.

cases.label: nchar(3) province codes: '', 'A', 'AB ', 'ABC', 'abc' (in another country) and 'é' come back padded to three characters
cases.reasoning: StateProvinceCode is nchar(3) (char(3) on PostgreSQL). Both engines pad with spaces on output; 'ABC' (US) and 'abc' (CA) are distinct values passed through with their own case. They are in different countries because the source key on (StateProvinceCode, CountryRegionCode) is case-insensitive. The empty string pads to three spaces on both, and is not NULL.

cases.label: several provinces of one country, ids with gaps and at the int limits, territory -2147483648, names with trailing spaces and an emoji
cases.reasoning: StateProvinceID jumps (0, 9, 2147483647); TerritoryID is not joined and is passed through at the int minimum. Three provinces share a country and a TerritoryID (a repeated non-key value). Names keep their trailing space; the emoji checks the load.

top-ties.detail: two rows of Person.StateProvince share CountryRegionCode = "US"

objections.text: The hand-derived fixed cases already test a lowercase province code joining 'US' under CI_AS and a province code with a trailing space joining its country. Additional mixed-case spellings and a combined case/trailing-space spelling attack the same two join mechanisms.
objections.resolution: A01 now uses non-ASCII Latin-1 and Greek case pairs and puts the combined case/trailing-space variant on the country side, exercising Unicode folding and asymmetric trimming paths absent from the hand-derived inputs.

objections.text: StateProvinceCode values 'ABC' and 'abc' for the same country collide under the source case-insensitive unique key on StateProvinceCode and CountryRegionCode. Those two source rows cannot coexist, so the case-only output portion is outside the source schema preconditions.
objections.resolution: A07 now places 'ABC' and 'abc' in different countries. Their composite source keys are distinct while the view still returns the stored case forms.
